title: Application architecture
speaker: Gera
notes: The browser sends a request to the shared C3L application. The module loader discovers index.js and mounts our router under /10-attendance. We did not change the shared router. Our router validates submitted data, calls AttendanceStore and returns HTML or JSON. The form and history views are separate JavaScript files, so the two interface tasks are small and independent. Shared layout and error-message helpers stay in pageLayout.js. My assigned backend area is recording, correcting and validating attendance. Nasir's area covers reading and filtering the records.

title: Database and class design
speaker: Gera
notes: We use Bun's built-in SQLite support. SQLite stores our attendance data in a local file, so we do not need a separate database server for this prototype. The attendance table stores an ID, course ID, student ID, calendar date, status, notes and update time. The unique combination is course, student and date. The save query inserts a record or updates status and notes when that combination already exists. The AttendanceStore class owns database access. Its main methods are save, list and close. There is one table at this stage. We have not invented relationships to other modules because shared user and course contracts are still pending. ACTION: Point to the unique key and AttendanceStore methods.

title: Validation and storage checks
speaker: Gera
lines: Course and student IDs: 1-50 characters after trimming
Real calendar date and one allowed attendance status
Optional notes: up to 300 characters
Bound SQL parameters and escaped HTML output
Storage failure returns a readable error
notes: Validation happens on the server as well as in the browser. IDs cannot be blank, the date must exist on the calendar and the status must be one of our three allowed values. Notes are optional and limited to 300 characters. SQL values are passed as parameters, and user text is escaped before it is displayed in HTML. A storage failure produces a readable error rather than a successful save message. Unit and storage tests cover invalid values, correction without duplication, filtering and persistence after reopening the database. Nasir will show the API and project evidence.

title: History filters and API design
speaker: Nasir
lines: GET /10-attendance/history serves the history interface
GET /10-attendance/api/attendance returns matching records
POST /10-attendance/api/attendance saves or corrects a mark
Filters: exact course/student IDs and inclusive from/to dates
Success 200, invalid input 422, storage failure 503
notes: My assigned technical area is reading and filtering attendance, API verification and regression testing. The history page uses the same stored records as the JSON API. Course and student filters match exact IDs. Both date limits are inclusive, and records are sorted newest date first. The JSON API supports GET for reading and POST for saving. The normal JSON success response is 200. Invalid fields return 422 and a storage failure returns 503. The HTML form uses a 303 redirect after saving so the browser opens the history page. I also coordinate requirement traceability and the update to the collaborative SRS.
